- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show excessive volatility and overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 79.99 → 82.95 → 83.93).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the latter half of the forecast window; prices often remain elevated longer than observed.
- Forecast bias is stronger when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 80s+), suggesting model overreacts to recent momentum.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after spikes; true outcomes show sharper declines than forecasted.
- Forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the first 10–15 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing downward pressure.
- Model does not adequately adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns; prices often remain flat or slightly rising despite true outcomes showing clear downward trends.
- Forecast accuracy improves as history includes more recent low prices (e.g., 65–70 range), suggesting model is sensitive to recent price context.
- Overshoots are more common in the middle of the forecast window (days 10–20), suggesting model overweights recent momentum without sufficient decay modeling.
